**Bottom line:** Adopt a managed identity provider (WorkOS, with Clerk a very close second) for the authentication primitives — sessions, credential storage, password reset, MFA — rather than building them in-house, while building tenant-scoping/authorization in the app regardless, since no vendor (bought or self-hosted) owns that layer. "No enterprise customers yet" turns out not to mean SSO/SAML is irrelevant — every vendor checked prices it near-zero today and the real cost shows up, concentrated and schedule-compressed, at the first enterprise deal. The buy-over-build call itself is robust (survives large swings in how the trade-off is weighted); the overall confidence is rated LOW only because of four cheap, specific open items (a WorkOS-vs-Clerk integration spike, a build/buy timeboxed spike, a sales-pipeline check on SSO demand, and a short audit of the existing tenant-mapping data) — not because the core recommendation is shaky.
